findings.F1: The weekly reversal the brief claims does not appear in folds B and C. On the 7-day grid, the slope of the next week's excess return on the past week's return is +0.0035 (t 0.12, 1,101 cells). Inside the tested profile there are only 60 cells, with slope t -0.18 and a mean excess of -2.38 %. In the choppy, high-swing tercile there are only 12 cells (slope +0.10, t 0.36).
findings.F2: A one-day fall is followed by a rebound the next day, graded with the size of the fall, but only when the coin is agitated. Agitated here means its 30-day swing is above its own median over the sample, which only approximates the profile's past-year median. The slope of the next day's excess return on the previous day's fall, both in units of the 30-day swing, is -0.206 when agitated (day-clustered t -3.17; 1,716 cases on 640 days). When calm it is -0.007 (t -0.07; 1,701 cases on 595 days).
findings.F3: Among agitated days, the graded rebound sits in falling markets and is absent in rising ones. Falling agitated: slope -0.302, t -3.02, 580 cases on 212 days. Choppy agitated: -0.506, t -2.40, only 73 cases on 56 days. Rising agitated: -0.040, t -0.39, 358 cases. Every calm cell has a slope of zero or the wrong sign: falling calm +0.04, choppy calm +0.31, rising calm -0.15 with t -1.34.
findings.F4: The rebound is on the fall side only.
findings.F5: The fall-side slope points the same way on every coin and in every year.
findings.F6: The rebound persists over three days and is still graded, but this reading uses overlapping, unclustered returns, so it is supportive only. Mean 3-day return: +1.40 % after falls of -2 swings or worse, +1.14 % after falls between -2 and -1 swings, and +0.36 % after smaller falls.
findings.F7: Against this backtest's cost of 0.19 % per trade, the one-day rebound is large. It is about 9 times the cost after falls of -2 swings or worse (1.82 %) and about 4 times after falls between -2 and -1 swings (0.75 %). The tested idea's unusual move was -0.39 % (t -0.40), about -2 times the cost.
findings.F8: Two other patterns do not stand out once their evidence is weighed.

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its usual daily swing, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: When a coin is swinging more than usual, a sharp one-day drop is a reason to buy for the next day, more so the sharper the drop, while in calm conditions the same drop is no reason to trade.
ideas.name: agitated one-day fall rebounds

ideas.idea: In a falling, agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its usual daily swing, the larger its rise over the next day.
ideas.consequence: In a coin that has been falling for two months while swinging hard, a sharp one-day drop is a reason to buy for a one-day rebound, sized up with the drop.
ideas.name: falling agitated daily rebound

ideas.idea: In an agitated market, the larger a coin's one-day fall relative to its usual daily swing, the larger its rise over the next three days.
ideas.consequence: A trader can hold a rebound after a sharp drop in a high-swing coin for three days, which spreads the trade's cost over a larger move.
ideas.name: agitated fall three-day rebound
